methods.label: Count the windows that cross a power of 5
methods.explanation:
For each \(m\), the number \(2^m\) lies in exactly one gap between consecutive powers of \(5\). It gives a valid pair precisely when \(2^{m+2}\) remains in that same gap. Thus we can count the starting exponents \(m\) whose window crosses a power of \(5\).

There are \(2012\) possible values of \(m\). No endpoint \(2^m\) or \(2^{m+2}\) equals a positive power of \(5\), since the former is even and the latter is odd. Also, a window \((2^m,2^{m+2})\) cannot contain two powers of \(5\): its endpoints have ratio \(4\), whereas two distinct powers of \(5\) have ratio at least \(5\).

Suppose
\[
2^r<5^j<2^{r+1}.
\]
Exactly two unrestricted windows cross this power, those starting at \(m=r-1\) and \(m=r\).

For \(1\le j\le866\), we have \(5^j\ge5>2^2\), and the given upper bound implies
\[
5^{866}<\frac{2^{2014}}5<2^{2012}.
\]
Hence \(2\le r\le2011\), so both excluded values \(r-1,r\) lie in the allowed range. These powers exclude \(2\cdot866\) windows.

The given power \(5^{867}\) lies between \(2^{2013}\) and \(2^{2014}\), so it crosses the windows starting at \(2012\) and \(2013\); only \(2012\) is allowed. Higher powers exceed \(2^{2014}\), and powers with nonpositive exponent are below every window.

All forbidden windows have therefore been counted, and none was counted twice. Each remaining \(m\) determines one \(n\), so the number of pairs is
\[
2012-2\cdot866-1=\boxed{279},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

review.mathematicalCheck: Each m determines at most one n. Every power 5^j for 1≤j≤866 excludes exactly two allowed windows, while 5^867 excludes only m=2012. Higher and nonpositive powers exclude none. A window has endpoint ratio 4, preventing duplicate exclusions by powers whose ratio is at least 5. The count is 2012−1732−1=279.
